editorial:
Set on death row in a Southern prison, this story pulls you into a tense, emotional world where a gentle giant named John Coffey carries a strange healing gift. Paul Edgecomb, the cell block's head guard, starts out doing his job, but Coffey's quiet power forces him to question mercy, justice, and what makes someone truly good. You feel the weight of every scene, from the small daily routines to the impossible choices, and the movie never rushes its big moments.

The acting is strong across the board, especially the calm, heartbreaking presence of Coffey and the steady leadership of Edgecomb. The pacing is slow but purposeful, giving you time to care before the hard turns arrive. It is long, so plan for a full evening, and some scenes are tough to watch. Still, if you want a powerful drama with a touch of fantasy, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the end, Paul realizes Coffey is innocent of the crime that put him on death row, but the system still moves forward. Coffey accepts his fate and asks Paul to carry out the execution. Before he dies, Coffey shares a vision of the real killers and heals Paul's painful infection one last time. Years later, Paul is still alive, far older than normal, carrying the guilt and mystery of Coffey's gift. The twist is that Coffey's power may have passed into Paul, leaving him with a long, lonely life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional dramas with a supernatural twist.
